content.text:
**I’d start with three parallel tracks: finish localization reporting, fix Brewfile export, and prepare unified Updates.** I checked live issues/PRs against current `main`.

| Track | Concrete next slice | Parallel fit |
|---|---|---|
| **Localization — [#142](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/142)** | Repair [PR #166](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/pull/166), then translate a bounded group of strings. CI crashes because its `metadata` test helper collides with Minitest; the PR also has a merge conflict. | Mostly scripts and localization files, independent of application logic. |
| **Brewfile export correctness** | Run export off the main thread and determine failure from the command result. Currently it can freeze the UI and miss errors whose output doesn’t begin with `Error:` or `fatal:`. | A small, useful bugfix. Separate operation controller from Updates, with some shared integration files. |
| **Unified Updates — [#147](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/147)** | First extract and test upgrade planning, wired into the existing upgrade action. Then build the combined formula/cask destination. | Planning and focused implementation can proceed alongside export; coordinate shared mocks and tests. |

The strongest code findings behind that recommendation:

- [Export failure handling](/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/cakebrew/Cakebrew/BPHomebrewInterface.m:829) discards command success and searches diagnostic text instead. A regression test should cover failed commands with empty or unfamiliar output.
- [Upgrade dispatch](/Users/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/cakebrew/Cakebrew/Controllers/BPInstallationWindowController.m:204) chooses formula versus cask from the first selected item. Unified Updates needs separate batches, distinct namespace identities, and an empty selection that runs nothing.
- The main view controller is now **1,513 lines**. A broad operations extraction under [#143](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/143) would overlap both features; keep that work focused on the upgrade seam for now.

There’s also existing work to finish: search [PR #165](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/pull/165) and its dependent fix [#167](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/pull/167) both have green CI. Complete their review/merge sequence before integrating new Updates navigation.

**Defer self-update [#149](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/149):** it explicitly depends on the first signed release in [#145](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/145), and the repository still has no releases.

Use isolated worktrees for the three tracks, coordinate shared controller/mock/test edits, and serialize UI runs. This was a read-only assessment; the export findings are source-confirmed, with runtime reproduction still needed.

from pathlib import Path
Path('/private/tmp/cakebrew-swiftui-swift6-issue.md').write_text('''## Goal

Migrate Cakebrew’s application code toward **Swift 6 language mode and SwiftUI**, modernizing package lists, the selected-package inspector and information popovers to follow macOS Human Interface Guidelines. Ship independently useful slices with behavior parity and measured performance. The first hosted SwiftUI view is the start of the migration, not completion of this epic.

## Current evidence

Inspected `main` at `c6a8d5a63d616b5659e8af4d96c0d54ccfcd30dd`:

- No tracked Swift sources, bridging header or Swift language-mode setting; startup remains `NSApplicationMain`. AppKit and Objective-C own the application today.
- More Information is a contained first surface: `Cakebrew/BPFormulaPopoverViewController.m` handles information/dependents content, with anchoring in `Cakebrew/Controllers/BPHomebrewViewController.m:803–826` and an existing UI journey. The general-information mode can move first while other modes retain their current implementation.
- Package lists are coupled to `BPFormulaeDataSource`, manager inventories, controller selection and Cocoa-bound menu enablement. Sorting, search cancellation, multi-selection, keyboard actions and context menus already exist and must remain functional.
- Selection restoration in `BPFormulaeDataSource.m:154–165` and stale detail-result checking in `BPSelectedFormulaViewController.m:114–121` compare names without namespace. Define identity as **package namespace plus full brew name**, never display name, row index or object address. A user-visible collision has not been reproduced; add deterministic same-name formula/cask tests.
- `BPFormula` is mutable, coded/copied and KVO/notification-driven. Do not expose it directly as transferable state across concurrent Swift tasks.
- #170 delivered namespace-safe selected-upgrade planning. The grouped Updates destination in #147, coherent item snapshots and truthful per-batch result presentation still remain.

## Migration approach

Use a small Objective-C/Swift boundary and host initial SwiftUI surfaces in the existing AppKit shell with `NSHostingController`/`NSHostingView`. Apple supports this incremental integration. Swift 6 language mode is selected per target and can interoperate with Objective-C; a new compiler alone does not establish Swift 6 language-mode adoption. [AppKit integration](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/appkit-integration), [Swift 6 migration](https://www.swift.org/migration/).

Keep UI state main-actor isolated; pass immutable, namespace-qualified snapshots across the boundary. Define cancellation, response-generation checks, callback lifetime and error mapping explicitly. Prove Objective-C imports, nullability, generated-header visibility and actor isolation with the first feature. Do not silence migration errors with broad unchecked Sendable or isolation escape hatches. [Incremental concurrency adoption](https://www.swift.org/migration/documentation/swift-6-concurrency-migration-guide/incrementaladoption/).

Retain macOS 15 compatibility unless a separate platform decision changes the minimum. Check individual API availability against that minimum. Preserve the unsandboxed Developer ID/hardened-runtime/notarization model, privacy protections and helper behavior. AppKit interoperability is acceptable where required for native behavior; document retained boundaries and their rationale.

## Ordered slices

- [ ] **Bounded feasibility spike:** prove mixed-language Swift 6 compilation and hosting for the real More Information path; measure a representative package-table prototype against current AppKit behavior. Record outcomes and availability limits, then discard spike code before production TDD.
- [ ] **First shippable SwiftUI feature:** migrate the general-information popover through the existing action and anchor. Include only the identity/snapshot/state adapter needed by this feature. Preserve selectable/copyable text, links, loading/error states and dismissal. Reject late responses after selection changes. Keep dependent-information modes working until their own migration.
- [ ] **Installed-package list:** introduce a native SwiftUI Table/List chosen from measured behavior, first for installed formulae and casks. Preserve namespace identity, multi-selection, selection across reloads/sorting, menu enablement, contextual actions, Return/Delete/double-click behavior and persisted sorting. Retain an explicit AppKit bridge temporarily if measured SwiftUI limitations prevent parity; track its exit criteria here.
- [ ] **Inspector and remaining popovers:** migrate selected-package details, dependency/required-by views and the remaining information modes. Give persistent detail content an inspector/panel presentation and reserve transient anchored popovers for concise contextual information. Share state contracts with the table without owning its implementation.
- [ ] **Catalog/search views:** extend the proven list to All Formulae/Casks, leaves, pinned and search results. Preserve the existing search coordinator, debounce/cancellation behavior, stable selection and 24-hour catalog cache.
- [ ] **Unified Updates:** implement #147’s grouped destination once using the new presentation components and the existing upgrade plan. Depend on coherent outdated-item snapshots and per-batch outcomes; do not build a disposable replacement AppKit Updates screen first. Preserve the existing namespace Outdated destinations until separately approved for removal.
- [ ] **Remaining application migration:** split Settings, services/tools, operation presentation, navigation/app lifecycle and owned backend/model code into feature-specific Swift 6/SwiftUI slices. Keep execution, cancellation, persistence, security and helper contracts intact; remove superseded Objective-C implementations as each replacement ships.
- [ ] **Completion audit:** inventory remaining owned Objective-C and AppKit UI, finish migration or explicitly document necessary interoperability exceptions, and verify the final application—not only its first SwiftUI view—meets the language, UI and behavior goals.

Each implementation slice gets its own acceptance criteria, owned files, expected failing test and PR. Track child issue/PR links in this epic rather than adding repository status documents.

## macOS design acceptance

- Lists use readable text, meaningful column headings, visible selection, sortable and resizable columns where useful, and clear package type/status/pinned indicators. Narrow windows and long package names remain usable; color alone never communicates status. Use native table/outline grouping for hierarchical data. [Lists and tables HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lists-and-tables).
- Popovers are concise, anchored to their source, content-sized and keyboard dismissible. Show one at a time; prevent nested popover chains and clipping. Keep extended or persistent information in an appropriate inspector/panel instead of an oversized transient surface. [Popovers HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/popovers/).
- Use system typography, spacing, semantic colors, SF Symbols and native controls. Follow the OS appearance and focus conventions; validate light/dark, increased contrast, reduced motion/transparency, keyboard navigation, contextual commands and VoiceOver. Support current SDK styling with availability-aware behavior on the minimum OS. [Designing for macOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-macos/).

## Verification and performance

- [ ] Production Swift targets build explicitly in Swift 6 language mode with concurrency diagnostics resolved; Objective-C compatibility does not stand in for Swift isolation guarantees.
- [ ] Unit tests prove same-name namespace identity, stable sorting/selection, immutable confirmation snapshots, stale-response rejection and cancellation/error behavior.
- [ ] Actual mixed-language app and test targets compile; focused tests have observed red/mutation evidence. Preserve full unit, mock-fidelity and UI coverage, adapting accessibility queries to user-visible behavior when implementation classes change.
- [ ] Independent UI review exercises the migrated user journeys, keyboard/context menus, accessibility, both appearances, resizing and long/localized content. Screenshots alone are insufficient.
- [ ] Before committing to the table implementation, record baseline and candidate initial render, scrolling, sort/filter latency, memory and brew-call counts on the same hardware with a representative full catalog and at least 10,000 synthetic mixed rows. Agree on explicit budgets from the baseline; do not invent unmeasured performance claims.
- [ ] Scrolling, selection and ordinary view recomputation initiate no per-row brew calls. Search debouncing, catalog caching and cancellation remain effective.
- [ ] Preserve all six localizations and formatting placeholders; coordinate new keys with #142’s translation work. Retain validated persisted settings/cache compatibility or supply explicit migration tests.

## Parallel work and dependencies

Start SwiftUI popover integration, the next #147 snapshot/Upgrade All work and stable-string localization batches in separate worktrees. Agree on the namespace/full-name identity contract first. The Updates owner owns manager/upgrade execution; the SwiftUI owner owns hosting/presentation; the localization owner reserves existing keys outside new UI text. One integrator owns edits to project registration, shared controller integration and shared UI tests.

After the first hosted feature proves the contract, list migration and inspector/popover modernization can proceed in parallel. Broad controller extraction under #143 must follow these feature boundaries rather than compete with them. Created [#173 — Swift 6 + SwiftUI migration and macOS UI modernization](https://github.com/scottdensmore/Cakebrew/issues/173).

I recommend **three parallel tracks**:

| Track | Next deliverable |
|---|---|
| **SwiftUI migration** | Move the general-information popover to SwiftUI, establishing the Swift 6 build and a small, tested Objective-C bridge. |
| **Unified Updates — #147** | Make Upgrade All capture an exact formula/cask snapshot, confirm that selection, and report each batch’s outcome. Reuse the upgrade planner we just shipped. |
| **Localization — #142** | Review and translate stable string batches, keeping new migration/Updates text separately owned. The reporting infrastructure is already complete. |

First, agree on package identity: **namespace + full package name**. Current name-only checks are unsuitable for mixed formula/cask lists.

After the hosting and state interface is proven, **list modernization and inspector/popover work can proceed independently**. Apple supports embedding SwiftUI incrementally in AppKit, so we can ship useful improvements throughout the transition. [Apple integration guidance](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/appkit-integration)

The migration issue explicitly covers sortable/resizable columns, native selection and keyboard behavior, VoiceOver, concise anchored popovers, appearance checks, and large-catalog performance. [Lists HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/lists-and-tables), [Popovers HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/popovers/)

I’d defer broad controller restructuring until these feature boundaries are established.
